title: Google is putting more links inside AI Search — here’s what changes

# Google is putting more links inside AI Search — here’s what changes


By OpenTools Team


·


October 18, 2026


Google is moving source links higher in AI answers, testing a dedicated official‑site box and expanding news carousels. The rollout could make it easier to leave the AI summary, but several pieces are still tests or phased releases.


##


Source links are moving higher in AI answers


Google announced on October 15 that it is increasing the number of inline links shown in AI Mode and AI Overviews and placing them higher in responses more often. These are the clickable words and phrases that send a searcher from an AI-generated answer to a source page.


The change matters because an AI summary can satisfy a question before a reader reaches the ordinary results below it. A link that appears beside the claim it supports gives the reader a clearer route to inspect the original page, see context and decide whether the answer left anything out.


Google did not publish a universal link-count requirement or promise that every claim will carry a source. The announcement describes a product direction, so readers should still open the cited page when the detail affects a purchase, health decision, deadline or other consequential choice.


##


A new official-site box is only a test


Google is also testing a dedicated section at the top of some AI responses for the one or two official pages that best complete a task. The box will explain why each link may be useful.


That could reduce a common search frustration: finding a government form, account page or manufacturer document among commentary and lookalike pages. It could also give official publishers a more visible path inside the AI interface.


The wording is limited. Google says it will test the display; it does not say that every user, country or query has it now. The feature should be treated as an experiment until it appears in a specific search session.


##


News carousels are expanding across more markets


Prominent carousels for timely articles are beginning to roll out to additional locations and languages around the world. Google says the carousels will also mark a user’s Preferred Sources when those publishers have relevant coverage.


Preferred Sources lets people choose outlets they want to see more often. Google says use of that feature has grown by more than seven times since the start of 2026, but it did not provide the starting number or a share of all Search users. The growth figure therefore shows momentum, not the feature’s total reach.


For readers, the practical test is simple: look for several independent reports when a developing story is uncertain. A more visible carousel improves discovery; it does not turn every included article into corroboration.


##


Creator names are becoming clickable in AI Mode


Google started testing clickable creator and publisher names on video results in AI Mode during the same week. The names open Search profiles that collect information about a creator and their broader work.


This adds identity context near a result without requiring a separate search. It can help distinguish an original channel from an account that reposts its material, although a profile is not an endorsement or a substitute for checking expertise and evidence.


Eligibility and setup are separate from the broader link changes. Google points creators and publishers to its Search-profile guidance rather than describing the profile test as a universal release.


##


The update makes the web more visible, but keeps Google in control


Taken together, the changes answer a recurring criticism of AI search: summaries can obscure where information came from and reduce the reason to visit the underlying page. Higher inline links and news carousels give people more exits from the generated response.


Google still decides which sources appear, where they appear and which interfaces reach each user. Publishers should measure actual referrals instead of treating visibility in an AI answer as traffic. Searchers should use the new links to inspect the source, especially when an answer compresses disagreement into one confident paragraph.


Follow major product changes on the[Google organization page](https://opentools.ai/organizations/google) .
